title: WPSS/1548/2019 of JAYA PANT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1548 of 2019
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Tej Singh Bisht, Deputy Advocate General for the
State of Uttarakhand/ respondents.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Petitioner is serving as Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade in
G.I.C. Banana, Block Bhimtal, District Nainital. She has been
transferred to Government Higher Secondary School Satbunga,
Block Bhimtal, Nainital vide order dated 25.06.2019. Thus,
feeling aggrieved, petitioner has approached this Court.
According to learned counsel for the petitioner, in terms
of Section 17 of the Transfer Act, petitioner had given her
option for Government High School Salyuda, Block Bhimtal,
District Nainital, however, her option was not considered,
although the post of Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade (English)
was vacant. He further submits that petitioner's husband is also
serving as Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade at Paharpani, Nainital,
who had requested for his transfer under spouse policy to Block
Bhimtal, however, the said request was also not acceded to.
Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
this Court thinks that ends of justice would be met, if petitioner
is permitted to make a representation to the Competent
Authority, which shall be decided by him, within some specified
time frame.
 Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of with liberty
to petitioner to make representation to Competent Authority
within one week from today. If such representation is made,
Competent Authority shall look into the matter and shall take
appropriate decision by passing a speaking order, in accordance
with law, within three weeks from the date of receipt of
representation alongwith certified copy of this order.
It is further provided that for a period of four weeks or till
decision on representation of the petitioner, whichever is earlier,
status quo shall be maintained regarding posting of the
petitioner.
Since, this Court has not considered the validity of the
transfer order on merits; therefore, it shall be open to the
petitioner to challenge the transfer order by filing another writ
petition, in case her representation is decided against her.
